why: resolveStatusFfa's win/lose decision must count players who are NOT ELIMINATED (dead AND out of stock), not players who are merely alive -- a player awaiting a scheduled respawn is dead this instant but still in the match. Reverting to a bare `alive` filter is exactly the pre-stock rule the FFA branch shipped with, and is the specific regression the task brief asked to be reviewed hardest for: it ends a stock match on the very first death. Caught by 2 of the 25 cases in versus-modes.test.ts: the N=2 regression test built specifically to discriminate the two rules (a 3+-player death leaves 2+ ALIVE tanks either way, so a larger N cannot tell them apart -- verified directly, an earlier N=3 draft of this same test passed under this mutation) and the mutual-kill-with-stock-remaining test, which this mutation reads as an immediate 'lose' instead of 'playing'.
killedBy: versus stock: a mid-stock death does not end the match the specific regression this feature is reviewed hardest for: a naive alive-count check ends the match on the FIRST death even with stock left -- ours must not
versus stock: elimination at zero stock a mutual kill where BOTH still have stock left is not a wipeout -- both respawn, still playing
